quests.question: ___ we reach the destination, the offices will have closed.
quests.hint: The offices close before arrival — they'll already be closed.
quests.explanation: 'By the time' introduces a time clause showing that one event will be completed before another happens. The offices will be closed at the point of arrival.

quests.question: Back up your files ___ the system crashes.
quests.hint: The crash is possible but not certain — you're taking precautions.
quests.explanation: 'In case' introduces a precautionary measure against a possible (not certain) future event. You back up to protect yourself if a crash occurs.

quests.question: ___ the results are confirmed, we will publish the report.
quests.hint: Publication follows immediately at the moment confirmation arrives.
quests.explanation: 'As soon as' means 'immediately when' or 'at the very moment that'. The publication will happen without delay once confirmation is received.

quests.question: ___ I was about to leave, the phone rang.
quests.hint: The timing was extremely precise — right at the moment of almost leaving.
quests.explanation: 'Just as' + past continuous expresses that two events happened at exactly the same time. 'I was about to leave' and 'the phone rang' were simultaneous.

quests.question: ___ the ceremony began, the rain suddenly stopped.
quests.hint: The rain stopping happened at the very same instant the ceremony started.
quests.explanation: 'Just as' highlights precise simultaneity. The two events — ceremony beginning and rain stopping — happened at exactly the same moment.

quests.question: He remembered her name ___ she disappeared into the crowd.
quests.hint: Remembering and disappearing happened at exactly the same instant.
quests.explanation: 'Just as' marks exact simultaneity. He remembered her name at the precise moment she disappeared — a perfectly timed, dramatic coincidence.

quests.question: The proposal is acceptable ___ it meets the legal requirements.
quests.hint: The acceptability is limited to one specific area — legal compliance.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' restricts the scope of the claim. The proposal is acceptable in the specific respect that it meets legal requirements — not necessarily in all other respects.

quests.question: ___ they were responsible for the decision, they must answer for its consequences.
quests.hint: Their responsibility is the formal reason they must face the consequences.
quests.explanation: 'Inasmuch as' introduces a reason based on degree or role. Their responsibility for the decision is the basis for requiring them to answer for it.

quests.question: The statement is accurate ___ it reflects the data available at that time.
quests.hint: The accuracy is qualified — it is true only within a specific scope.
quests.explanation: 'Insofar as' qualifies a statement. The statement is accurate only to the extent that it reflects the available data — implying limitations may exist.

quests.question: The new system is better ___ it processes data more quickly.
quests.hint: The improvement is defined by one specific characteristic.
quests.explanation: 'In that' means 'because of the specific fact that' or 'in the particular way that'. It pinpoints exactly in what respect the system is better.

quests.question: His approach differs from hers ___ he prefers collaboration over independent work.
quests.hint: The difference is being specified precisely — not just stated generally.
quests.explanation: 'In that' specifies the exact point of difference. It answers the question 'in what way?' — the difference lies specifically in how they prefer to work.

quests.question: The two policies are similar ___ both aim to reduce carbon emissions.
quests.hint: The similarity is being defined by one shared characteristic.
quests.explanation: 'In that' defines exactly how the two policies are similar. It focuses on the specific shared characteristic rather than making a general claim.

quests.question: The report was thorough, ___ it lacked a conclusions section.
quests.hint: The report was good overall — but had one specific shortcoming.
quests.explanation: 'Except that' introduces a specific exception to a general positive statement. The report was thorough except for one particular omission.

quests.question: I would have agreed, ___ the financial terms were unacceptable.
quests.hint: You were almost ready to agree — one thing stopped you.
quests.explanation: 'Except that' introduces the single obstacle that prevented agreement. Everything was fine except the specific issue of the financial terms.

quests.question: The agreement was satisfactory ___ one clause remained ambiguous.
quests.hint: There was one exception to the general satisfaction — formally expressed.
quests.explanation: 'Save that' is a formal/literary equivalent of 'except that'. It introduces a single qualification or exception to an otherwise positive or complete statement.

quests.question: ___ the contract has expired, we are free to negotiate new terms.
quests.hint: The expiry of the contract is a new fact that creates a new freedom.
quests.explanation: 'Now that' links a recently established fact to its consequence. The contract expiring is the new situation that enables fresh negotiation.

quests.question: ___ you have the authority, why not make the decision yourself?
quests.hint: Having the authority is the observable reason for the suggestion.
quests.explanation: 'Seeing that' means 'given the fact that' or 'since'. It introduces a present observable situation as justification for the suggestion.

quests.question: ___ she has passed all the required tests, her licence should be issued.
quests.hint: Passing the tests is an established prerequisite — the conclusion follows logically.
quests.explanation: 'Given that' introduces a known fact or premise from which a logical conclusion follows. She passed the tests — therefore the licence should be issued.

quests.question: ___ complex a system is, ___ difficult it is to maintain.
quests.hint: Increasing complexity leads to increasing difficulty.
quests.explanation: The structure 'the + comparative...the + comparative' shows proportional relationship. Greater complexity directly causes greater maintenance difficulty.

quests.question: ___ less sleep you get, ___ worse your concentration becomes.
quests.hint: Two things change proportionally — but in opposite directions.
quests.explanation: 'The less...the more/worse' is a proportional structure where one thing decreasing causes another to worsen. Less sleep leads directly to worse concentration.

quests.question: ___ earlier you report the problem, ___ easier it will be to fix it.
quests.hint: Earlier reporting makes fixing easier — a proportional relationship.
quests.explanation: The 'the + comparative...the + comparative' structure shows that the degree of one thing affects the degree of another. Early reporting makes fixing progressively easier.

quests.question: Call me ___ you arrive — I'll be waiting.
quests.hint: The arrival is certain — the question is only at what moment it happens.
quests.explanation: 'When' is used when the event is certain to happen. 'If' suggests uncertainty. The caller is expected to arrive, so 'when' is correct.

quests.question: Take a spare battery ___ your phone dies during the journey.
quests.hint: The phone dying is possible but not certain — it's a precaution.
quests.explanation: 'In case' introduces a precaution against a possible (not certain) event. The battery is for safety — you don't know if the phone will die.

quests.question: ___ I were offered that role, I wouldn't accept it.
quests.hint: This is a hypothetical situation — the offer is not real or likely.
quests.explanation: 'If' introduces a hypothetical condition in a second conditional. 'Were' signals the unreal/hypothetical nature of the condition. It is not something likely to happen.

quests.question: Wait here ___ the doctor is ready to see you.
quests.hint: Waiting continues right up to the moment the doctor is ready.
quests.explanation: 'Until' marks the end point of a continuous action. The waiting doesn't stop until the specific event (doctor being ready) occurs.

quests.question: ___ she arrived at the station, the train had already left.
quests.hint: The train left at some point — and she arrived after that point.
quests.explanation: 'By the time' is used when one event is completed before another event happens. The train's departure was already complete at the time she arrived.

quests.question: Please finish reading ___ we begin the discussion.
quests.hint: Reading must be completed first — discussion comes second.
quests.explanation: 'Before' specifies that the reading must occur prior to the discussion. Unlike 'until' (which marks an end point of a continuous action), 'before' marks a prior action.

quests.question: ___ the new software was introduced, productivity improved significantly.
quests.hint: The software introduction was the trigger — productivity improved from that point.
quests.explanation: 'Once' means 'as soon as' or 'after the point at which'. The productivity improvement followed immediately from the software introduction.

quests.question: The lecture was so engaging ___ no one looked at their phones.
quests.hint: 'So' sets up a degree-result structure — one word completes it.
quests.explanation: 'So...that' expresses an extreme degree and its consequence. The lecture was so engaging (extreme degree) that nobody looked at their phones (consequence).

quests.question: ___ much she tried, she could not open the jar.
quests.hint: No amount of effort helped — the trying was in vain.
quests.explanation: 'However much' means 'no matter how much'. It introduces a clause showing that the degree of effort made no difference to the outcome.
